set_language_desc: English is the source language. Other languages are community translations and may be incomplete; missing text falls back to English.
set_sus_su_desc: Deprecated entirely on SuSFS v2.0.0+ kernels; the toggle is a no-op there.
set_hide_cusrom_desc: Searches /system, /vendor, /system_ext, /product and top-level /data for custom-ROM name strings and hides matches (sus_map + sus_path_loop). Higher = fewer file-type exclusions. Extreme also scans /data dalvik-cache, resource-cache and misc — thorough but slow, and hides more, so use only if a check still detects the ROM.
set_hide_injections_desc: Maps every file a module injects — files under each module’s system/ overlay and *.so under /data/adb/modules — so an inode/memory-map scan can’t spot them. Needs the SUS_MAP kernel feature.
set_hide_custom_recovery_desc: Hides leftover TWRP/OrangeFox/install-recovery traces (/data/recovery, install-recovery.sh, storage folders) when present.
set_hide_suspicious_pty_desc: Hides /dev/pts/0–5, the pseudo-terminals a root shell allocates. Off by default — can affect terminal apps.
set_hide_addon_d_desc: Hides the addon.d directory of survive-OTA scripts (e.g. 50-lineage.sh) that name a custom ROM.
set_hide_framework_res_desc: Maps framework-res.apk overlays under /system, a common resource-overlay detection point. Needs the SUS_MAP kernel feature.
set_hide_data_local_tmp_desc: Hides every entry under /data/local/tmp — the usual staging area for root tools and installers.
set_hide_nonstd_sdcard_desc: Hides top-level /storage/emulated/0 folders that aren’t standard media dirs (DCIM, Download, Android…). Broad — hides any stray folder you keep in storage root. Off by default.
set_hide_nonstd_sdcard_android_desc: Hides /storage/emulated/0/Android entries that aren’t data, media, or obb.
set_hide_lineage_strings_desc: ⚠ Risky. Redirects SELinux policy (sepolicy.cil, file_contexts) and lineage-mentioning .rc files to empty fakes. These are policy/init files — if something re-reads them at runtime you can hit SELinux denials or a service that won’t start. Leave off unless a check specifically needs it and you understand the risk. Needs the open_redirect kernel feature.
set_skip_kernel_umount_zygisk_desc: When ReZygisk or ZygiskNext is installed, let it handle unmounting instead of the kernel umount — they do their own, and doing both conflicts. Only takes effect when one of them is present; otherwise the module unmounts normally. On by default.
set_disable_add_try_umount_desc: Deprecated in SuSFS v2.0.0 — the add_try_umount backend was removed, so this has no effect on v2.0.0+ kernels (Nyx unmounts through KernelSU’s built-in kernel umount there). Only relevant on older kernels that still expose CONFIG_KSU_SUSFS_TRY_UMOUNT. Advanced — off by default.
set_umount_zygote_desc: Deprecated in SuSFS v2.0.0 — the command was removed, so this is a no-op on v2.0.0+ kernels (the built-in kernel umount covers isolated services). On older kernels it can break modules that overlay framework files; boot into rescue mode if you bootloop.
set_disable_bin_update_label: Skip binary update check on open
set_disable_bin_update_desc: On by default. Turn it off and opening the WebUI compares the installed susfs binary against the published one, then offers to install it — nothing is ever replaced without asking.
set_bin_update_now_desc: Compares hashes against sidex15/susfs4ksu-binaries. Works whether or not the check on open is enabled.
about_credits_intro: NyxSUSFS is a from-scratch WebUI and script layer built to sit on top of ksu_module_susfs's config layout, so it stays a drop-in for anyone already using it.
about_credits_susfs: SuSFS by simonpunk is the kernel magic that makes all of this possible. None of this exists without it.
about_credits_sidex15: ksu_module_susfs by sidex15 is the original module Nyx grew out of. Nyx keeps its config layout so it stays a friendly drop-in for anyone already using it, and ships sidex15's ksu_susfs binaries. Huge thanks for the foundation.
about_credits_brene: A number of Nyx's mount-hiding ideas were sparked by studying BRENE by rrr333nnn333. The ideas were reimplemented in Nyx's own way, but the inspiration deserves a shout-out.
about_credits_rezygisk: The Zygisk-aware unmounting and mount-source detection were guided by the ReZygisk project (PerformanC), thanks for the pointers on doing it right.
about_credits_poqdavid: Everything else, the WebUI, the targeted hiding, the glue, I built myself, with love for the community. Issues and translations welcome. Prop spoofing now lives in its own module, NyxProps.
home_susfs_inactive_hint: Confirm your kernel is SuSFS-patched, then reboot.
